sth_longwood_curator.text: The rooms are small and low, and Napoleon hated them. The house was rat-infested and damp when he arrived. The British added a room for his billiards and he refused to use it for years in protest.
France bought the house in 1858. The French consul is the official guardian. In a way, you are standing in France.

sth_longwood_valet.text: His bedroom is as it was. The camp bed he took on campaigns. A bath. A clock stopped at the time he died, which is a sad little touch and also entirely true.
People ask if he was poisoned. A great many books have been written. Most doctors now think it was stomach cancer, like his father.
